articles.summary: Paulina Porizkova reveals how lifting heavy and Pilates transformed her severe anxiety and strength after bilateral hip replacement surgery.
articles.body: Paulina Porizkova is enjoying the benefits of exercising after starting to work out. In a recent Instagram post, the 61-year-old supermodel shared her gym routine with her many followers, and shared working out has helped her in more ways than one. "I really used to hate to work out. And so I didn’t do it until I was in my 40s, and I realized that it really helped with my pretty severe anxiety," she said in a voice-over footage of her lifting weights. "And also it made me look better." She explained that while she still doesn't like working out and would "much rather be reclining on the couch and reading novels," that would help "feed my brain, but it doesn’t really do it for my body," so she chooses to go to the gym. She explained that she's taken the advice of doctors and Instagram influencers and tries "to lift heavy," adding that she also mixes Pilates into her routine. In the video, Porizkova can be seen doing exercises such as hammer curls, cable pulls, deadlifts, pull-ups, lunges and others. "What's wonderful about it is, it not only helps my severe anxiety and makes me look better, but it also has made me a lot stronger," she added. articles.title: K-pop star Sunmi loves Notion and ear cleaning videos
articles.summary: Nearly 20 years into her music career Wonder Girls’ Sunmi is staying humble, but persistent.
articles.body: Sunmi is an undeniable force in K-pop. She first made her debut as a member of the Wonder Girls back in 2007, one of the first K-pop acts to really break through in the West. The English version of their single “Nobody” was the first K-pop song to hit the Billboard Hot 100 in October 2009. In 2010 Sunmi left the group to go back to school, but the siren call of a music career pulled her back in. She released her debut solo EP Full Moon in 2014. That began a run of award-winning releases for the pop star, including Song of the Year for “Gashina” at the Gaon Chart Music Awards. Despite her near-constant presence in the K-pop world as a solo artist and as a member of the Wonder Girls, whom she rejoined in 2015, Sumni only just released her first solo LP, Heart Maid, in 2025. This year she released the single “Forever July,” which blends ’90s R&B synths with rubbery bass and UK garage-inspired drums. Sunmi has called it one of her most personal songs. And she wasn’t afraid to get personal in our Q&A either, revealing details about her writing process, her greatest disappointment as an artist, and her love of ear cleaning videos. What is your most indispensable tool? My phone. I use the Notes app and Voice Memos a lot when I’m writing lyrics or making music. Whenever I have a good idea, I can immediately pull it out and write it down, so I really can’t live without it. Which is the most underappreciated? The Samsung Galaxy series. It has made my work environment so much easier. Team Galaxyyyyyy! What is the first app you install on a new phone or computer? These days, you can transfer all the apps and data from your previous device, so I don’t really have to install anything separately. But if that process didn’t exist, I’d probably install KakaoTalk, a messaging app, first. What is one thing you wish you could change about your phone? I have so many unnecessary photos and screenshots in my gallery. I wish there were a feature that could recognize similar or duplicate photos and group them together, so I could delete them all at once. What sites do you have pinned to your tab bar? Notion. I use it a lot because I work on many group projects. It’s convenient, but it takes quite a long time to get used to. I think the UI could use some improvement. How many tabs do you have open right now? Four: Notion, Google Drive, YouTube, and Claude. Which social media platform do you use the most? I don’t really use social media that much, but I think I use Instagram and X the most. What is your happy place online? Videos of people getting their ears cleaned on YouTube. What is your favorite gadget you’ve ever owned? I’m not really good with technology, but I think the Samsung Z Fold 8 that I’m using right now is probably my favorite device. I often need to work on documents or edit videos while I’m on the go, and it’s incredibly convenient. I can work with both hands on a wide screen, and it’s surprisingly light. It’s exactly the kind of device I’ve always needed. What game do you have the fondest memories of? MapleStory by Nexon. I played it when I was in elementary school, and even after becoming an adult, I would sometimes play the mobile version. The graphics really bring back memories of my childhood. Which tech trend do you wish would go away? Deepfakes. Ew. What is one thing you wish you had created? Stranger Things 5 and Game of Thrones 8. What creation are you most proud of? “Tail.” It’s a song that still gets me excited every time I perform it live. When I hold my breath, the audience holds their breath too, and when I explode, they explode with me. It creates this really unique experience. Which are you least proud of? “You Can’t Sit with Us.” It was the first song where I ever tried rapping. But the lyrics and even my voice were terrible. What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received? Always stay humble. You should never let yourself become arrogant. What is your current obsession? I really love ice cream. Korean summers are shockingly hot, so it’s hard to survive without ice cream. I absolutely love Salt & Straw’s Salted Caramel Waffle Cone, but there’s nothing quite like it in Korea. What do you do when you need to focus? I find a small space to organize my thoughts. What do you do when you’re feeling stuck? I say “No?” out loud. For example, if I start thinking to myself, “I can’t do this,” I immediately say “No?” out loud. When was the last time you went somewhere without your phone? When I’m shooting, I leave my phone with my manager. Even during short breaks, I barely look at my phone. But I’ve never actually gone somewhere without my phone. What’s the last piece of physical media you bought? The Senses of an Everydayist, a new essay collection by lyricist Kim Eana. articles.title: Sydney Sweeney y Marilyn Monroe comparten un inesperado vínculo familiar: ¡primas novenas en una generación!
articles.standfirst: Lo descubre una investigación genealógica y viene de la rama del padre
articles.summary: Lo descubre una investigación genealógica y viene de la rama del padre
articles.body: Sorpresas que da la vida. A veces se dice que la vida es un pañuelo, pues se ha encontrado un vínculo especialmente llamativo. Sydney Sweeney y Marilyn Monroe tienen más cosas en común de las que muchos imaginaban. Más allá de las constantes comparaciones por su imagen y su proyección en Hollywood, una investigación ha encontrado un sorprendente nexo entre ambas actrices: ¡comparten raíces familiares! Los genes... El hallazgo ha sido realizado por MyHeritage, una plataforma especializada en genealogía, que ha concluido que la estrella de Euphoria y el gran icono del cine estadounidense coinciden en la misma línea familiar por parte de padre. Es más, dicha empresa ha hecho un estudio que las sitúa como primas novenas con una generación de diferencia. Roi Mandel, que es el director de investigación de la compañía, explicó que el estudio nació por las continuas comparaciones entre ambas figuras de Hollywood. "La gente siempre ha establecido paralelismos entre Sydney Sweeney y Marilyn Monroe, pero comprobar que existía una conexión real en su árbol genealógico nos llevó a profundizar en los archivos", explicaba. Según dicho estudio efectuado, el vínculo entre ambas mujeres se remonta varios siglos atrás. Los investigadores identificaron a Ezra Perry, un colono inglés que vivió entre 1625 y 1689 y se estableció en Massachusetts, como el antepasado común de las dos intérpretes. Por todo ello, la investigación sostiene que Steven Sweeney, padre de Sydney Sweeney, y Charles Stanley Gifford, padre de Marilyn Monroe, descienden directamente de Perry. Esta conexión convierte a ambas actrices en primas novenas, aunque con una generación de diferencia. La coincidencia resulta todavía más llamativa porque Sweeney nunca ha ocultado su admiración por Monroe. La actriz estadounidense ha hecho referencia en varias ocasiones a la leyenda de Hollywood y a la influencia que ha tenido en la cultura popular. En los Governors Awards de 2025, Sweeney llamó la atención al aparecer con un peinado inspirado en Los caballeros las prefieren rubias, una de las películas más emblemáticas de Marilyn Monroe. Ahora, gracias a esta investigación, aquel parecido que muchos seguidores señalaban desde hace tiempo no se limita a la imagen o al éxito en la gran pantalla, sino que también tiene una explicación que se remonta más de tres siglos atrás.

articles.title: When Nana Patekar revealed he didn't have money to pay for his father's treatment so he died in the hospital: 'That hesitation stays with you'
articles.summary: Veteran actor Nana Patekar, who passed away on Thursday, October 8, leaves behind a remarkable body of work and a legacy that extends beyond his
articles.body: Veteran actor Nana Patekar, who passed away on Thursday, October 8, leaves behind a remarkable body of work and a legacy that extends beyond his performances on screen. Over the years, the actor has also offered glimpses into the personal experiences that shaped him. One such moment was when he opened up about the painful loss of his father, whom he could not afford to get treated.Reflecting on his early struggles, Nana spoke about how his financial situation gradually improved after he entered the film industry. However, by the time he began earning well, it was too late to save his father, who passed away in a hospital when the family could not afford his treatment."I started earning money from films. Initially, I earned a little, and then I started earning a lot. But when my father was ill, I didn't have the money to pay for his treatment, and he died in the hospital," he recalled in an interview with NDTV in 2024.The actor also revisited the difficult nights he spent outside the hospital with a friend while his father was admitted. Unable to stay inside overnight, the two would sit on the stairs or the footpath, playing Antakshari as they waited anxiously for news about his father's condition."We used to sit on the stairs or on the footpath outside the hospital. We weren't allowed to stay inside overnight, so we would sit outside and play Antakshari. My friend was there with me. You never knew when someone would come out and tell you that your father was no more," Nana said.Looking back, the actor expressed the regret of not having enough money to secure better medical care for his father. Despite achieving considerable success in his career, the memory of being unable to help his father during his final days continued to affect him emotionally."If I had had the money, I could have got him better medicines and taken him to a better hospital. But I couldn't do that. That hesitation stays with you. Even today, when I remember those days, my eyes fill up with tears," he added.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. "We know the difficulties of this game, as Frosinone are a very direct team, they have a lot of enthusiasm and a high press."

This is also because Napoli had a tough fixture list, losing back-to-back games with Como and Inter, plus a disappointing 1-1 draw against Fiorentina.

"Now we have nine games in a row between Serie A and the Champions League. We dropped points with a few errors, if you have the right determination on the ball, you can score more goals, but if you don't have determination at the back, then you struggle to defend too," added Allegri.

articles.title: Traditional dolls set to catch eyeballs at Navaratri Bombe Habba
articles.summary: Chikkamagaluru Navaratri Bombe Habba starts Oct 11 at Ranganna Kalyana Mantapa, showcasing traditional doll displays; entry free for 9 days.
articles.body: Chikkamagaluru: For nine days, stories of gods, kings, glimpses of village life and contemporary society will come alive in miniature form, not on a stage but on tiers through beautifully arranged dolls. This is the unique charm of Bombe Habba.To preserve the rich traditions, art and history associated with Navaratri, the Chikkamagaluru District Brahmin Mahasabha will organise a nine-day Navaratri Bombe Habba at Ranganna Kalyana Mantapa from Oct 11. District president P Manjunatha Joshi described the event as more than just an exhibition. “It is a living museum of our culture and heritage,” he told reporters on Friday.According to Joshi, the tradition of displaying dolls during Navaratri occupies a special place in Karnataka’s cultural heritage. “Kings and maharajas used to install and worship Pattada Bombe, or royal dolls, in their palaces. What began as a royal custom gradually spread to ordinary households during the reign of the Mysore rulers,” he said.A practice once confined to palaces has now become an integral part of celebrations in homes across the region.Last year, seven renowned Bombe Manes -Anjanadri, Andal, Doopadakol, Mysuru, Myurashilpi, Kanaka Shankaregowda and Jaji - showcased their collections at the venue. Organisers expect even greater participation this year, with more families displaying treasured heirloom dolls passed down through generations.A Bombe Mane is much more than a collection of dolls. Each tier narrates a distinct story.The lower steps typically depict scenes from everyday life, including markets, villages, weddings and farming activities. The middle tiers feature themes such as Ashtalakshmi, social messages and contemporary issues, while the topmost levels showcase deities, scenes from the Puranas and the Pattada Bombe, symbolising royal authority and prosperity.“The exhibition will feature displays on the worship of deities, stories from the puranas, social and artistic themes, the significance of Pattada Bombe, village life and contemporary issues,” Joshi said. The highlight of this year’s exhibition will be a pair of intricately carved sandalwood dolls representing a king and queen, he added.Entry to the exhibition is free.
